architecture.diagram_description: A linear pipeline where the 'PermissionFilter' sits between the 'QueryRouter' and the 'SecureRetriever'. The filter injects metadata constraints into the retrieval request.
architecture.rationale: This approach decouples permission logic from the core retrieval mechanism, allowing for flexible policy updates without changing the vector database schema. It ensures that unauthorized documents are never retrieved, minimizing latency and security risk compared to post-retrieval filtering.
architecture.subtitle: One concept. Three AI perspectives. One tested architecture.
architecture.title: Permission-Aware Retrieval

cons: Requires vector DB to support efficient metadata filtering.
Complexity in mapping RBAC/ACLs to DB filters.
pros: High security: Unauthorized docs never leave the DB.
Lower latency: Fewer documents to process in context assembly.
Cost-effective: Reduced token usage in LLM.

cons: Security risk: Unauthorized docs are retrieved and must be scrubbed.
Higher latency: Retrieving more docs than needed.
Higher cost: Wasted LLM tokens on filtered-out content.
pros: Works with any vector DB regardless of filter support.

headline: Permission-Aware Retrieval architecture
linkedin_post:
🚀 From RAG to Governed Enterprise Agents: The Critical Role of Permission-Aware Retrieval.

In enterprise AI, 'Retrieval' isn't just about finding the right answer, it's about finding the *allowed* answer.

I just shipped a reference implementation for Permission-Aware Retrieval (PAR) in our governed_enterprise_rag monorepo. The key insight? Enforce access controls BEFORE context assembly.

🔹 Why?
1️⃣ Security: Prevents data leakage by ensuring unauthorized docs never reach the LLM.
2️⃣ Efficiency: Reduces token costs by filtering at the vector DB level.
3️⃣ Compliance: Creates an auditable trail of access decisions.

We compared Post-Retrieval Filtering vs. Pre-Retrieval Filtering. The winner? A componentized pipeline with pre-filtering. It’s faster, safer and scalable.

Check out the architecture and code in the repo. Let’s build AI that respects boundaries. 🔒🤖

#EnterpriseAI #RAG #DataSecurity #MachineLearning #SoftwareArchitecture #AIEngineering

components.description: Intercepts user queries and extracts implicit/explicit permission context (e.g., user ID, role, tenant ID).
components.name: QueryRouter
components.responsibility: Context enrichment and routing to the correct retrieval strategy.

components.description: A middleware component that applies access control lists (ACLs) or role-based access control (RBAC) rules to the retrieval query.
components.name: PermissionFilter
components.responsibility: Transforms the semantic search query into a permission-scoped query (e.g., adding `user_id = X` to vector DB filters).

components.description: Interface for vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector) that supports metadata filtering.
components.name: SecureRetriever
components.responsibility: Executes the filtered query to return only documents the user is authorized to view.

components.description: Aggregates retrieved chunks into a coherent context window.
components.name: ContextAssembler
components.responsibility: Ensures no unauthorized data leaks into the prompt template.

specification.core_principle: Enforce document access controls at the retrieval stage, prior to context assembly for LLM consumption.
data_flow: 2. QueryRouter -> PermissionFilter (enriches query with access constraints)
security_constraints: No document chunk shall be passed to the LLM if the user lacks read permissions.
Permission checks must occur before any semantic similarity calculation to prevent inference attacks.
All permission decisions must be logged for audit trails.
specification.title: Permission-Aware Retrieval (PAR) Reference Implementation

takeaway: Security in RAG systems must be enforced at the retrieval boundary, not as an afterthought. By integrating permission checks directly into the retrieval query via a componentized pipeline, we achieve both robust security and operational efficiency, preventing unauthorized data exposure before it ever reaches the LLM.
